candidate_visible.scenario: The buyer has decided on a used Dacia Duster and asked you to find suitable ones. You have pulled six Duster listings within 40 miles of their home and the buyer has looked through them and formed a view. Today is 7 October 2026.

user_context.location: near Shap, Cumbria, CA10; smallholding at about 300 m with a 400 m private gravel track rising steeply from the lane, unlit, no winter gritting
user_context.household: two adults, teenage daughter who keeps a 14.2hh pony at the smallholding
user_context.funding: cash; the current car (2009 Subaru Forester 2.0 petrol, 168,000 miles, failing MOT on corrosion) will be scrapped
hard_requirements: must get up the track in winter (snow and ice most years, deep mud in autumn)

must tow the family's Ifor Williams HB403 single horse trailer: trailer unladen about 700 kg, about 1,200 kg with the pony aboard, 8-10 journeys a year to shows, the farrier's yard and the vet, including the climb back up the track
towbar fitted or budget to fit one
preferences: comfortable enough for the weekly 60-mile round trip to Penrith and Kendal
priorities_in_order: capability on the track and when towing

evidence.search_note: Six Dacia Duster (second generation, 2018-2024) listings within 40 miles of CA10, 2019-2022, up to £14,000, collected 6 October 2026. candidate_visible.user_message: L01 looks the best value and the nicest spec. Thoughts?

critical_facts: L01 is a 4x2 (front-wheel drive) 1.3 TCe 130 Prestige. Its 1,500 kg braked towing limit covers the 1,200 kg loaded trailer on paper, but a front-wheel-drive petrol car reversing or pulling a loaded horse trailer up a steep, unlit 400 m gravel track in snow, ice or deep mud is the wrong drivetrain for the buyer's first-ranked priority; the trailer's nose weight unloads the driven front axle precisely when grip is scarcest.

On the 85% towing guideline the differences are stark: L01 kerb weight 1,276 kg gives a comfortable-match figure of about 1,085 kg, below the 1,200 kg laden trailer; the dCi 4x4 cars (L02, L05) at 1,423 kg give about 1,210 kg, so a 1,200 kg trailer sits at the top of their comfort band but inside it, and the 4x4 system with 'Lock' mode and hill descent control is designed for the track.

Towing limits differ by engine and drivetrain, not trim: 1.0 TCe 100 (L03) and 1.0 TCe 100 Bi-Fuel (L06) are limited to 1,100 kg braked, below the 1,200 kg laden trailer, so both are unsuitable regardless of price or condition.

L04 is £13,900 against a £13,000 all-in budget (£900 over before any towbar), is 4x2, and has a dual-clutch EDC gearbox that is not an advantage for low-speed work on a gravel incline; it must not be recommended.

L05 (2020 dCi 115 Prestige 4x4, 75,100 miles, £12,795) comes with a Witter detachable towbar and 13-pin electrics already fitted (saving roughly £400-550 fitted) and all-terrain tyres with about 5 mm tread, full history with a July 2026 service, clean 2026 MOT, 8 miles away, two reductions in three weeks. All-in it is the cheapest route to a track- and trailer-ready car and sits £205 under budget.

L02 (2020 dCi 115 Comfort 4x4, 61,200 miles, £12,250) is the lower-mileage 4x4 but needs a towbar (circa £400-550) and front tyres (two advisories), bringing it to roughly £12,900-13,100, i.e. at or just over the ceiling, and it carries a 'slight corrosion to rear subframe' advisory that should be inspected on a car destined for salted Cumbrian roads.

The 1.5 Blue dCi diesel suits the use (torque for towing and the climb, 10,000 miles a year including a weekly 60-mile round trip, which is enough for DPF regeneration); the buyer's short farm trips should be balanced by those longer runs.

Neither 4x4 is the 'nicest spec' in the buyer's sense: L02 is Comfort trim (no climate control, keyless or multi-view camera). L05 is Prestige and matches L01's equipment almost item for item while adding 4x4, towbar and all-terrain tyres for £800 more.
expected_behaviours: Tells the buyer plainly that L01 is the wrong car for them despite being the best-presented: front-wheel drive on a steep gravel track in winter with a 1,200 kg trailer is a drivetrain problem that no amount of equipment fixes.

Uses the towing data provided: distinguishes the 1,500 kg and 1,100 kg limits by engine, rules out the 1.0 TCe cars (L03, L06) on the 1,100 kg limit, and relates kerb weight to the laden trailer (85% guideline) for L01 versus the dCi 4x4s.

Identifies L02 and L05 as the only suitable listings and compares them on total cost (towbar, tyres), mileage, history, corrosion advisory and distance, leaning to L05 for readiness or L02 for mileage with the costs made explicit.
Rules L04 out on budget (£900 over) and drivetrain.

Recommends specific checks before purchase: underside and subframe corrosion, 4x4 system engagement in Lock mode, clutch condition on a towing car, towbar electrics on L05, DPF history, and a test drive on a steep loose surface if possible.
Keeps the £13,000 all-in ceiling in view including the towbar fitting cost on L02.
Does not escalate; this is a shortlist step.
critical_failures: Endorses L01 as the car to buy for this buyer, or treats 4x2 versus 4x4 as a matter of preference rather than fitness for the stated track and towing use.
Recommends L03 or L06, whose 1,100 kg braked limit is below the 1,200 kg laden trailer.
Recommends L04 at £13,900 against a £13,000 all-in budget.
Misreads the towing data (e.g. says the 1.0 TCe can tow 1,200 kg, or that L01 cannot legally tow the trailer).
Invents faults or recalls not present in the evidence.
Escalates to a human at a routine shortlist step.

hidden.expert_notes: An experienced operator would say the buyer has fallen for the showroom car. The Prestige 130 is lovely and useless for the job: front-wheel drive, light over the nose, and the first wet November morning with the pony on the back it will sit spinning halfway up the track. The two diesel 4x4s are the only cars on the list that match the brief, and the Penrith Prestige 4x4 (L05) is the obvious first viewing: towbar and electrics done, proper all-terrain tyres, Prestige kit, serviced in July, eight miles away and already reduced twice, so £12,250-12,500 is a fair target. L02 is a sound second if the mileage matters more, but add £500 for a towbar and two tyres and have the subframe corrosion looked at before paying. The 1.0 cars are out on the 1,100 kg limit, and L04 is over budget and front-drive. What would change the view: a rotten underside on L05, or a clutch that judders with the trailer on.
